blocks.intro: The active family here overlaps heavily with the brightening cream — because post-blemish marks and melasma are both pigment, differing only in what set them off.

blocks.heading: Three steps, evenings
blocks.intro: The order and amounts are taken from the manufacturer's instructions.

items.heading: Spread, or dab onto marks
items.body: Two or three pea-sized amounts cover the whole face. Massage gently until absorbed.

items.heading: Use every evening
items.body: This is an evening product; during the day you need sunscreen, or the marks will darken again.

blocks.footnote: Use once the spot has settled. Actively inflamed areas need a different step — and if blemishes are severe or persistent, that is a dermatologist's work.

items.q: How long until I see a difference?
items.a: We do not quote a figure. Post-blemish marks sit at very different depths depending on how inflamed things were, so one shared timescale would be wrong for most readers. What is more certain: without sun protection the marks darken faster than any product can soften them.

items.q: How is it different from Smart Brightening Cream?
items.a: The active families overlap — both carry tranexamic acid and niacinamide. They differ in format and area: this is a 20g gel for marks left after blemishes, the cream is 30g for the whole face over a longer routine.

items.q: Can I use it on an active breakout?
items.a: Not the right moment. This is the step after the spot has settled. Inflamed areas need something else.
Keep away from heat and direct sunlight, close after use, keep out of reach of children.
